o: Unconjugated bilirubin bound to plasma albumin fraction
Free lipid-soluble bilirubin crossing cell membranes freely
Indirect-reacting bilirubin passing through renal filters
Delta-bilirubin covalently linked to circulating globulins
Conjugated bilirubin diglucuronide regurgitated into blood

qs.q: A surgeon notes that a patient's total serum bilirubin must exceed a certain threshold before jaundice clinically becomes visible as yellow sclerae. What is this approximate threshold?
qs.e: Jaundice becomes clinically visible when serum bilirubin rises above approximately 35 micromol/L (2 mg/dL), whereas normal total bilirubin is under 17 micromol/L (1 mg/dL). Sclerae show the yellow discolouration before the general skin.
